title: Article 359 — Suspension of the enforcement of the rights conferred by Part III during emergencies

content.overview: Article 359 empowers the President, while a Proclamation of Emergency is in operation, to declare by order that the right to move any court for the enforcement of such of the rights conferred by Part III (except Articles 20 and 21) as may be mentioned in the order, and all proceedings in any court for the enforcement of the rights so mentioned, shall remain suspended for the period during which the Proclamation is in force or for such shorter period as may be specified. The order may extend to the whole or any part of India. Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended (44th Amendment). Every such order is to be laid before each House of Parliament.
content.glance: President may by order suspend enforcement (not the rights themselves) of specified Part III rights during Emergency — except Arts 20 and 21, which cannot be suspended. Order laid before Parliament.
content.study:
Article 359 ordered suspension of enforcement:
- Not automatic (unlike Art 358 for Article 19 in war/external-aggression Emergency).
- Presidential order naming the rights whose enforcement is suspended.
- Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended (44th Amendment safeguard).
- Suspension of the right to move court / pending proceedings for those rights.
- May cover whole or part of India; duration of Proclamation or shorter.
- Laid before each House of Parliament.

Examination: enforcement vs existence of rights; Arts 20–21 non-suspendable; contrast Art 358; parliamentary laying.

sections.heading: Key rules
sections.body:
1. Presidential order may suspend enforcement of specified Part III rights during Emergency.
2. Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended.
3. Suspends right to move court and related proceedings for the named rights.
4. Order laid before each House of Parliament.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Explain Article 359.
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 359, while a Proclamation of Emergency is in operation, the President may by order declare that the right to move any court for the enforcement of such rights conferred by Part III as are mentioned in the order (except Articles 20 and 21) and all proceedings in any court for the enforcement of those rights shall remain suspended for the period of the Proclamation or a shorter specified period. Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended. Every such order shall be laid before each House of Parliament.

examTips: Ordered suspension of enforcement; Arts 20–21 never suspended; contrast Art 358.

keyTakeaways: Art 359: Presidential order suspending enforcement of specified FRs (not 20/21).
